premises.text: Retailers change prices rapidly and less transparently, including personalized prices that make consumers pay more
premises.evidence_span: They're changing prices faster and faster and less transparently than ever before

premises.text: Store price-protection policies are too complex and time-consuming for consumers to use, so refunds go unclaimed
premises.evidence_span: Not only are the policies often complex by design, it takes a ton of time to price compare, figure out if you're owed money back

premises.text: Paribus automatically detects purchases and price drops and files claims against store policies on the user's behalf
premises.evidence_span: when we think you're eligible for a claim, we'll check it against our internal database of official and unofficial store policies

premises.text: The company charges only after successful savings, typically 25% of recovered money
premises.evidence_span: The only time that Paribus earns is after we save you money first

value.text: Get shoppers refunds they are owed without lifting a finger
value.evidence_span: Almost $45 more dollars in my pocket, and I didn't have to lift a finger

causal_links.evidence_span: use your own data against you to get you to pay more through custom prices
automatically file a claim on your behalf, as if you were to send it yourself
charged 25% of the money we earn you

notes: Split pricing abuse vs claim-hassle as separately revisable market assumptions. Inbox OAuth/security/store-count folded into automated-claim product. Demo Xbox story used only as illustration. Singletons retained with notes that each can fail independently.
